title: Posterior inferotemporal neuron activities during a visual fixation task and a visual tracking task.
abstract: Single neuron activities were recorded from the posterior inferotemporal cortex (PIT) while a monkey was fixating or tracking a target spot. Of 168 recorded neurons, 86 were activated by the extrafoveal slit stimuli; 48 were activated during eye fixation. Twenty were activated only during tracking, and not by fixation or a extrafoveal slit stimuli. It was suggested the PIT participates not only in the perception mechanisms but also in the foveation mechanisms such as fixation or tracking.
